strongest_confirmed_findings: New extraction, not new October balance: June30 pledged GPU/related assets were $1.487112B in the Microsoft VIE, while $938M gross debt was funded/issued and no customer operating-lease revenue had commenced. Horizon1 acceptance in August limits extrapolation of June pre-acceptance status into October.

The financing documents explicitly allocate failed-acceptance collateral and refund shortfall risk to IREN under a limited parent guarantee. Replacement demand must also meet customer, term, financing and rating criteria. This is more specific than a general claim that idle chips lose value.

Separate $3.657072B construction in progress and $107.068M hardware prepayments concern infrastructure development and undelivered mixed AI/mining hardware, respectively. Neither measures paid-for usable idle chips.
NVIDIA is a confirmed $3.4B IREN customer in the May7 release and August27 10-K. May26 Dell disclosure alone cannot establish this identity, and the Dell guarantee is by IREN, not NVIDIA.
investable_read_through: Customer fee protection starts with acceptable delivered capacity. Before acceptance, resale shortfall and upfront refunds can reach IREN parent; replacing a customer requires lender-quality terms, not just demand. No current impairment or short thesis established.
contradictions_to_prior_assumptions: Do not erase September16 review. Supersede current compute-attribution assumption and date/source locators through this review and atomic deltas.
May26 source limitation in October8 NVIDIA research remains correct for that exhibit; the broader claim that NVIDIA identity is unknowable would conflict with May7 release and FY26 10-K.
Split >$20M signed-contract claim from ~$25M discussions instead of publishing them as a realized range.
Do not equate $3.657B infrastructure CIP, $107M undelivered hardware prepayments or $1.487B pledged book value with paid-for idle chips.
